codec.encode_rule: both encoders emit varint64(offset) then varint64(size): while value > 0x7f emit (value | 0x80) low byte and shift right 7; emit the final low byte. EncodeTo(char*) returns the pointer one past the last byte and does no bounds checking. EncodeTo(std::string*) assembles the same bytes in its stack frame (scratch at rsp, stack canary at rsp+0x18) and appends them with std::string::_M_append after a max-size guard (0x3fffffffffffffff - current size) that throws std::length_error ("basic_string::append") instead of appending
codec.leaf_rule: GetVarint64Ptr(p, limit, *value): null when p >= limit at entry or when the input ends mid-varint; per byte, a set continuation bit ORs (byte & 0x7f) << shift into the result, then shift += 7 and the decode fails when shift exceeds 63 (so a continuation bit on the 10th byte fails); a clear continuation bit ORs byte << shift, stores the result and returns p + 1. At shift 63 only bit 0 of the last byte survives the shift, on both the failing and the storing path.
codec.wire_format: varint64(offset) followed by varint64(size); unsigned LEB128, 7 bits per byte, low groups first, continuation bit 0x80 on all but the last byte of each varint; at most 10 bytes per varint
